question:
A 64-year-old man with hypertension seeks medical attention for progressively worsening and
increasingly frequent headaches. As a hedge fund manager, he experiences prolonged work hours,
reduced sleep, and work-related anxiety affecting his ability to fall asleep. The osteopathic structural
examination reveals hypertonicity in the suboccipital muscles. The patient demonstrates limited ability
to bring his chin toward his chest during active range of motion testing. The occipitoatlantal (OA) joint
shows restricted translation from right to left. What is the correct diagnosis for this patient's OA joint
dysfunction? Answer Choices: (A) FRLSL (B) ERRSR (C) FRRSR (D) ERRSL (E) FLRSR (F) ERLSL
(G) ERLSR (H) FRRSL (I) FRLSR (J) FLRSL
 A. FRLSR
B. FLRSR
C. FRRSR
D. FLRSL
E. FRRSL
F. ERLSR
G. FRLSL
H. ERRSL
I. ERRSR
J. ERLSL
